perspective:
Harold Padilla’s available information:

- He feels frustrated and anxious because his project is not progressing well; he believes his team is unmotivated.
- He arranges and attends a coffee-shop meeting with his friend/advisor Arthur. He knows Arthur as someone whose advice he relies on.
- He hears Arthur advise that motivation is tricky, that Harold should understand each team member’s individual drives, that people need to feel valued and understood personally, and that one-on-one conversations may help.
- Harold tells Arthur he has mostly focused on project goals/deadlines and agrees to try the one-on-one approach. He leaves feeling hopeful and relieved.
- Harold tells his team he wants quick one-on-one chats to understand what motivates each of them. He hears Team Member 1 say it could be helpful and Team Member 2 say they are open to it. Harold says he will schedule time and asks them to make the project a success together.
- Later, Harold observes that the team still is not responding well. He feels disappointed and worried about the project’s future.
- He meets Arthur again and tells him the suggestions did not work. He hears Arthur suggest there may be deeper issues: personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors, and that Harold may need to dig deeper. Harold says he had not thought of that and decides to hold another round of meetings.
- Harold then meets with team members one-on-one. He tells them he has noticed performance issues and asks about concerns.
- Team Member 1 tells Harold there is tension between a few people that is affecting work. Harold says he will look into resolving conflicts and asks if there is anything else.
- Team Member 2 tells Harold they feel overwhelmed by the workload and stressed, making motivation hard. Harold says he will see if tasks can be redistributed and that their well-being is important.
- Harold feels optimistic and empowered. He tells the team he will implement regular feedback sessions and team-building activities to create a more supportive environment.
- He hears Team Member 1 say that sounds great and will help them work better together. He hears Team Member 2 agree and say it is good their concerns are being addressed.
- Harold tells the team their input and well-being are crucial and asks them to work together to make the project a success.

Harold does not have access to anyone’s unspoken thoughts, private motives, hidden conflicts, or future outcomes beyond what he directly observed and was told.
